description: PULP APB3 GPIO F5 behavior plus two named dir-resolved pad groups over the same PADIN word: the host drives the groups in declaration order, each for its own declared window, before the case's own CPU work. The F5 facts are the reviewed PULP GPIO sequence.
notes: the F5 facts are the reviewed sequence of configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-gpio-pins-f1f5.json: GPIOEN(4)=0xffffffff, INTEN(24)=1, INTTYPE_LOW(28)=1 (pin 0 rise) and PADOUT(12)=0x2b, with INTSTATUS(36) as the read-clearing status word

the two groups address the one pad word the bound gpio.pins endpoint exposes (PADIN at offset 8): PADDIR(0) is still zero in the cases that carry them, so both groups declare inout and the device's own dir port decides bit by bit. A group naming a second pad word would need a second pad port on the model and is refused by name, not merged

group0 'phase_low' declares external_value 0x00001111 and holds it for 2 host ticks; group1 'phase_high' declares 0x00002222 and, being the last group, keeps the wire for the rest of the case. The order in this file is the order the host drives: phase_low first, then phase_high

the external values are stimulus facts, not device facts: they are what the host drives while the device's dir bit is low, and the case line states which group presented which word and how many ticks it held it
no execution is claimed by this file: the run under runs/p2-pins-serial-20261103/ is the evidence
